facts: Both Criminal Appeal filed by the State of Haryana and Special Leave Petition filed by accused Fatta Ram, are directed against the judgment and order dated 03.05.2012 passed by High Court of Punjab and Haryana...
Prosecution story, in brief, is that Vakil Singh (deceased in the present case) was an accused in the case of murder of one Atma Ram of Village Nagal.
...Vakil Singh succumbed to the injuries and died in the hospital.
After committal of the case, Sessions Judge, Kaithal, framed charge against all the three accused in respect of offences under Section 302, 323 read with Section 34 IPC...
PW-8 Balbiro has narrated the prosecution story stating that her husband was accused in connection with murder of Atma Ram, and he was acquitted by the Court.
Statement of PW-2 is corroborated not only from the medical evidence on record discussed above but also from the statement of PW-7 Tehla Ram.
issues: Whether the High Court erred in law in disbelieving the testimony of injured eye witness (PW-8) and that of Tehla Ram (PW-7) as against Bira @ Bhira.
Whether the presence of accused Bira @ Bhira who was Son-in-law of Atma Ram, and belonged to a separate village appears to be doubtful.
petitioner_arguments: It is argued that the High Court has erred in law in disbelieving the testimony of injured eye witness (PW-8) and that of Tehla Ram (PW-7) as against Bira @ Bhira.
It is contended that the evidence of the prosecution witnesses is equally reliable as against Bira & Bhira, as it was reliable against the two other accused.
respondent_arguments: The High Court has taken note of the fact that Atma Ram (in whose murder case Vakil Singh was accused) was father of accused Sant Lal.
Role of Sant Lal in commission of crime to take revenge after the acquittal of the deceased, cannot be doubted.
Involvement of Fatta, as he was caught by the villagers immediately after the incident, can also not to be doubted.
court_reasoning: We do not find sufficient reason to disagree with the above view taken by the High Court.
Therefore, we are not inclined to interfere with the acquittal of Bira @ Bhira recorded by the High Court.
holding: The Criminal Appeal and the Special Leave Petition are hereby dismissed.
